answer: Require time-staked reputation that accrues only from sustained, verified work: an agent earns trust gradually over weeks, and that standing cannot be bought, transferred, or cloned. Like tending an orchard, value grows through seasons of consistent output, so spawning a thousand fresh identities buys no influence. A sudden delta in activity or output triggers review, and the old fable of strength in numbers fails, because each fake identity must pay the same slow time cost as a real one before it can vote, earn, or transact.
